text: DSH Subagent Model Router 是面向 Web 客户端的子代理模型路由插件。它在 DSH 注册模型目录、配置工具和按模型别名委派的 subagent_model 工具，可为每条路由设置标签、用途说明及推理强度，并支持前台或可继续的后台任务。用户可在 Subagent Models 设置页维护路由，也能在会话界面查看子代理使用的模型；可选 Better Sidebar 集成提供子代理列表。适合希望按任务分配不同模型并跟踪委派工作的 DSH 用户。需要先在 DSH 配置可用模型路由和执行后端；插件自身未声明 API 密钥。

DSH Subagent Model Router lets DSH Web users configure model aliases and delegate tasks with selected models and reasoning effort. It supports foreground or background subagents, a wait tool for results, and a settings page for routes. Session UI shows model identity.
我想让 DSH 根据任务难度把子任务交给不同模型，并为每次委派选择推理强度。
怎样配置可选模型别名，让 DSH 把需要处理的工作委派给对应的子代理模型？
I want to track which model handled each delegated DSH task and collect the results of background subagents.
DSH Subagent Model Router 的功能「按路由委派子代理」：为模型配置别名、provider、model 和可选推理强度后，subagent_model 按所选别名启动任务；可配置前台等待结果或后台继续运行。
DSH Subagent Model Router 的功能「管理子代理模型设置」：在 Web 的 Subagent Models 设置页添加、编辑或删除模型路由，并调整委派深度与后台执行选项；保存后通过插件设置端点更新当前配置。

> [!NOTE]
> This is the maintained continuation of [CypherNaught-0x/DSH-Subagent-Model-Router](https://github.com/CypherNaught-0x/DSH-Subagent-Model-Router), including [poka-IT's DSH 0.1.7/0.2.0 port](https://github.com/CypherNaught-0x/DSH-Subagent-Model-Router/pull/3). It targets DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x and adds per-task reasoning effort. Full history and credit are preserved.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · DSH Subagent Model Router：Stop using one model for every kind of work. Configure your preferred fast, affordable, specialized, and high-reasoning models once; the router gives your agent the aliases, tags, and guidance it needs to intelligently select the best route for each delegated task.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · DSH Subagent Model Router：That means faster routine work, stronger results on difficult problems, better control over cost, and less model micromanagement. Subagents can run in parallel, their results are reliably joined before the parent responds, and the model chosen for each task stays visible throughout the UI.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Why use it?：- **Better results where they matter** — reserve your strongest models for architecture, security, deep reasoning, or critical review.
- **Lower cost and latency** — send routine searches, edits, and focused implementation work to faster or more economical routes.
- **Automatic, task-aware routing** — friendly aliases, capability tags, and plain-language usage guidance help the orchestrator choose intelligently.
- **Per-task reasoning effort** — the orchestrator can run the same route at `low` for mechanical work or `xhigh` for a stubborn bug, with an optional default per alias.
- **Confident parallel delegation** — launch multiple specialists in the background and reliably collect every result before synthesis.
- **Clear model visibility** — see which model actually handled a task in subagent headers and in the optional Better Sidebar **Sub-agents** tab.
- **Easy setup** — configure your model team from the Web UI, through a guided skill, or directly in a Cordis patch.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Why use it?：> [!TIP]
> Already using [Better Sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar)? The router adds an optional **Sub-agents** tab through Better Sidebar's public `registerTab` API.

text: dsh-subagent-model-router README · Build your ideal model team：*Define friendly routes and tell the orchestrator when each model shines—from quick, budget-friendly tasks to your most demanding work.*

dsh-subagent-model-router README · What it adds：- `subagent_model`: a delegation tool whose `model` argument is restricted to user-configured aliases, with an optional `reasoning_effort`.
- `wait-for-subagents`: a join tool that waits for this agent's outstanding continuable background children, including standard and model-routed delegations, and returns their terminal results.
- Per-model tags and routing descriptions embedded in the tool schema and system prompt.
- `model_subagent_catalog`: a read-only view of models advertised by registered LLM providers.
- `configure_subagent_models`: a model-facing tool that reads or replaces only this plugin entry's configuration, without filesystem access.
- `model-subagent-setup`: a guided skill for selecting routes, generating routing guidance, obtaining confirmation, and saving through the constrained configuration tool.
- **Settings → Subagent Models**: a Web settings page for manually adding, editing, and removing routes.
- A hot-reloaded plugin configuration: the `config:` of the `- id: dsh-subagent-model-router` Loader entry in a Cordis patch.
- Foreground execution and durable continuable background subagents.
- Configurable stale-s

dsh-subagent-model-router README · What it adds：With an empty `models` list, the catalog, configuration, and wait tools remain available alongside the settings page and setup skill, but `subagent_model` is not registered. This provides a bootstrap state for initial setup.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：When model-selectable delegation is available, the system prompt tells the orchestrator not to duplicate work it delegated. After issuing all intended background delegations, it must call `wait-for-subagents` before synthesizing the child results or giving a final answer. While a same-session completion goal is active, the orchestrator must not merely report that another model is handling the task and end its turn with background subagents still outstanding: ending the turn triggers immediate goal continuation and can race child tracking. Waiting joins the outstanding work so the orchestrator can synthesize the results and continue or complete the goal. The wait tool joins every continuable background child started by that parent through `subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `subagent_model`, or `auto_agent_run`; it remains useful when no model routes are configured. It reserves standard, forked, and project-specialist delegation calls before they can publish a child, and after plugin reload it discovers direct continuable children when their durable descriptors confirm their mode and the live Agent is either running or interrupted wi

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：Direct human steering must not leave the parent blocked in an old join. When a committed `agent/inbox/spliced` event inserts a `source.kind: user` message at `next-step` for that parent, an active wait returns `{ kind: "interrupted", pending: [...] }` without cancelling or consuming any child. Each pending entry carries the exact child and run identity when available. The DSH agent loop does not automatically schedule a second tool call after the parent answers. Instead, the plugin's system prompt, tool description, and interruption result explicitly require the parent to answer the steering message first and then call `wait-for-subagents` again before final synthesis. That second call resumes the retained records and returns their eventual terminal output; queued `next-turn` input, model-authored context, cancellations, and events for other sessions do not trigger this outcome. A simultaneous child completion remains retained for the resumed wait.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：The continuation manager's durable settlement notice triggers immediate reconciliation when a terminal lifecycle event was missed. Recovery requires matching post-boundary evidence in both the retained child epoch log and the parent notice, so an absent registry entry or an idle/resumable child is never treated as success by itself. For an ordinary tracked start, the record remains bound to the exact child and run identity. After plugin reload, a genuinely running child can instead be discovered without a published run id; its exact retained Agent object plus child and parent log boundaries identify that observed activation safely. A ten-second watchdog provides the same reconciliation as a fallback if the live notice event was also missed. Cancellation still rejects the active tool call without consuming records, and parent disposal still releases tracked children and active waits. If another plugin already owns or scope-shadows the `wait-for-subagents` name, this plugin leaves it untouched and suppresses its wait-specific guidance and tracking for the affected agents.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：An interrupted child can be idle with queued input that will not run until explicitly resumed. The wait returns `{ kind: "paused", pending: [...], paused: [...] }` for an exact live child with parked input and an aborted activation suffix, including when discovered after reload. It does not settle the child, discard its queue, or wake it automatically. Address the paused state explicitly: if work should continue, use `send_message` with appropriate instructions, then call the wait again; otherwise report the pause and request direction. Do not blindly restart intentionally interrupted work or repeatedly re-wait. All pending records remain joinable. An idle child without parked input, or a child still running, is not classified this way.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：As a defense in depth for Harness versions affected by the continuable ownership-hold ordering bug, the router rejects a model tool call that uses `send_message` to target its own calling agent id. The rejection happens in the public `tools/execute` waterfall before the built-in tool calls the subagent service, and a resident child receives its direct parent id in the error hint. This deliberately narrow guard does not replace the core fix: it cannot protect direct subagent-service callers, reject every other invalid resident relationship, or repair ownership state already corrupted in the current host process. Deploying this source requires the normal plugin rebuild/reload (or a host restart); an already-corrupted process still requires a host restart.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：`listingInactivityTurns` keeps old continuable children from crowding model-facing discovery. For each direct parent, the router counts incoming human messages (or parent-agent relay messages for nested agents) and resets a child's window whenever that child receives a parent/user message. Once the configured number of turns passes without contact, `list_agents` omits that child. This is presentation-only: the durable child is not deleted, unloaded, or made unaddressable, so a known id still works with `send_message` and can reappear after contact. Set the option to `0` to disable filtering. After a router reload, children without reliable process-local contact history receive a fresh visibility window rather than being hidden on incomplete evidence.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Orchestrator behavior：If a committed manager settlement notice exists but the exact retained result is unavailable, corrupt, or inconsistent, watchdog reconciliation reports a diagnostic error rather than fabricating output or waiting forever. The immediate notice path leaves room for the normal terminal event to arrive first. Plugin unload explicitly rejects active waits and releases tracker state and watchdog timers.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Reasoning effort：`subagent_model` accepts an optional `reasoning_effort`, matching the built-in DSH `subagent` tool. Effort ids are adapter-owned: each exact route advertises its own levels (for example `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`), so the router does not hard-code a list.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Reasoning effort：- **Precedence:** the call's `reasoning_effort`, then the alias's `reasoningEffort`, then the selected model's own default. The parent's effort is never inherited, because an alias names its own route (DSH applies the same rule when a `subagent` call changes route).
- **Preflight:** an explicit or alias-default effort is validated with the LLM runtime's `resolveCallConfig` before any child is created. An unsupported level fails immediately and the error lists the supported ones.
- **Discovery:** the router reads each configured route's levels with `resolveModelInfo` and shows them in the tool description and system prompt, for example `{default effort: low; efforts: none|low|medium*|high|xhigh|max}`, where `*` marks the model default. Lookups re-run when the configuration or the registered LLM adapters change; a route that cannot be resolved is shown without levels and never blocks registration.
- **Resume:** the effort becomes part of the child's Agent options, so a continuable child resumed with `send_message` keeps it.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Reasoning effort：To expose one model at two efforts with different routing guidance, configure two aliases on the same route:

```yaml
      - alias: luna-quick
        provider: cliproxy-openai
        model: gpt-6-luna
        reasoningEffort: low

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Model identity chips：The opened subagent header and every row of the Better Sidebar **Sub-agents** tab show the configured friendly display name for the latest adapter-resolved request, falling back to the model id when that route is not in the current router settings. Hover and accessible text expose the complete `provider/model` route. The plugin resets the route at the child's own descriptor so a fork cannot inherit its ancestor's model, and it omits the chip until the child records an authoritative request route.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Model identity chips：The native subagent catalog in the session header (`subagent-catalog`) belongs to DSH and shows no model chip; the router no longer replaces it.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Model identity chips：When Better Sidebar is installed, the router registers a single-instance **Sub-agents** tab with `betterSidebar.registerTab({ id, title, component, single, order })`. The tab reads each parent's `subagentCatalog` Session projection from the Sessions service list, loads it with `sessions.refreshProjections()` for the root and every expanded branch while visible, renders nested children with model identities, and opens a child through `uiWorkspace.openSession()`. Registration is scoped with `ctx.inject(['betterSidebar'], ...)`, so the native router never waits for the optional service; late service load and unload are handled automatically. The native Better Sidebar controls which tab is selected and currently restores its Start page after refresh; use the `+` menu to reopen **Sub-agents**. (The optional bottom workbench has separate persistence semantics.) When the service is absent, the integration is inert.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Compatibility：| Plugin version | DeepSeek Harness | Configuration store |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0.10.0` | `0.1.7-rc.2` through `0.2.x` (verified daily on `0.2.0-rc.2`) | Loader entry `config:` in a Cordis patch |
| `0.9.0` | `0.1.7-rc.2` and later `0.1.7` builds | Loader entry `config:` in a Cordis patch |
| `0.8.0` and earlier | `0.1.0-rc.6` to `0.1.6` | `subagent-model-router` section of `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` |

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Compatibility：DSH 0.1.7 removed `settings.yaml` and the `ctx.settings.register()/get()/watch()` API. A plugin now declares a Config schema whose fields are `.volatile()`: DSH commits a changed value into the running plugin and emits `loader/volatile-update` instead of remounting it, and the Settings service (`ctx.settings`) exposes those fields as a form addressed by the plugin's Loader entry id. This release therefore:

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Compatibility：On first boot, DSH 0.1.7 renames `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` to `settings.yaml.imported` and imports each section into the entry whose id matches the section name. The old `subagent-model-router` section does not match the entry id `dsh-subagent-model-router`, so it is not imported: move it by hand into a Cordis patch as shown in [Configure through a Cordis patch](#configure-through-a-cordis-patch).

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Compatibility：DSH 0.2.0 no longer exposes `Agent.inbox.hasPending`; the router detects parked input from the public `inbox.nextTurn`/`inbox.nextStep` lists and still accepts the older flag.

DSH 0.1.7 also caps a parent at 8 active continuable children (`maxActiveSubagents` of the Host `subagent` entry). A background `subagent_model` call beyond that cap fails with `ACTIVATION_LIMIT_REACHED`; wait for a child to finish or raise the cap.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `0.1.7-rc.2` or later, including `0.2.x`
- The Web profile and built-in subagent conversation UI
- A preset exposing the normal skill loader/tool
- The Host `spawn` subagent provider, included by standard DSH profiles
- Optional: a compatible `dsh-better-sidebar` release exposing the public `registerTab` API (including the native right-sidebar surface)
dsh-subagent-model-router README · Install：```sh
dsh-subagent-model-router README · From GitHub：dsh plugin --profile web add github:pumbleblock/dsh-subagent-model-router

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Or from inside this checkout：dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

Restart `dsh web` after installation and refresh the page. Open **Settings → Subagent Models**, or invoke:

```text
/model-subagent-setup
```

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through the Web UI：The page talks to a package-owned, same-origin Host endpoint (`/dsh-subagent-model-router/settings`) backed by the DSH Settings service, with schema validation, provider-capability validation, and revision conflict protection. Saving writes the `config:` of the `- id: dsh-subagent-model-router` entry in the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml`; the change applies live: the old delegation tool is removed and the updated schema and prompt guidance are registered immediately. The router turns off the Settings service's generated form for its entry so the same fields are not edited from two pages.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through the Web UI：A home patch (`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`) or a `--patch` overlay applies after the profile patch. When one of them sets this entry, the Settings service refuses the write and the page shows an error that names both files; edit the overriding patch instead.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through the Web UI：The endpoint rejects non-loopback transport and cross-origin mutations by default. A trusted loopback reverse proxy may allow specific browser origins with the comma-separated `DSH_SUBAGENT_MODEL_ROUTER_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` environment variable, for example `https://dsh.example.test`. Requests must still arrive over loopback, and each mutation Origin must exactly match both the request Host and an allowlisted origin.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through the model-facing tool：- `action: "get"` reads the current normalized settings.
- `action: "update"` replaces the complete model list and optionally changes the backend, depth, or background policy.
- The tool calls the Settings service directly and can modify only its own Loader entry (`dsh-subagent-model-router`, or the id it is mounted under); it accepts no filesystem path and cannot read or write other entries.
- Updates pass the same schema and provider-capability validation as the Web UI, persist to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, and apply live.
- An update fails with an explicit error when the Settings service is not loaded, or when a home patch or `--patch` overlay overrides the entry.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through the model-facing tool：The update action is intentionally documented for direct user-requested changes only. The setup skill must show the complete proposed list and receive explicit confirmation before calling it.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through a Cordis patch：Put the configuration in the `config:` of the plugin's Loader entry. The entry already exists (the bundle mounts it), so the patch names only its `id`. Use the home patch `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (default `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml`) to configure every profile at once, or a profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` to configure one profile:

```yaml
- id: dsh-subagent-model-router
  config:
    subagentProvider: spawn
    maxDepth: 3

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through a Cordis patch：See `examples/cordis.patch.yml` for a copyable patch. A patch entry's `config:` replaces the entry's whole config, so list every field you set. With `"patchReload": "live"` in the profile's `package.json` (the web profile default), DSH reloads edited patches while running and the router applies the new routes without a restart; with `"startup"` the change applies at the next launch. An invalid edit is logged and the previous routes stay active.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Configure through a Cordis patch：A configuration in the home patch or a `--patch` overlay takes precedence over the profile patch, so Web UI saves and `configure_subagent_models` updates are refused while it is present (see above).

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Settings reference：| Field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models` | `[]` | Routes exposed to AI agents. An empty list leaves setup/catalog only. |
| `models[].alias` | required | Stable selector shown in the tool's `model` enum. |
| `models[].provider` | required | Exact registered LLM provider route. |
| `models[].model` | required | Exact model id interpreted by that provider. |
| `models[].displayName` | alias | Human-readable label in routing guidance. |
| `models[].tags` | `[]` | Lowercase kebab-case routing tags. |
| `models[].description` | required | One sentence describing when to use this route. |
| `models[].maxTokens` | provider default | Optional cap for an initially created or resident child. DSH rc.6 did not restore it after a continuable child was cold-resumed; not re-verified on 0.1.7. |
| `models[].reasoningEffort` | model default | Optional default effort id for this alias, validated against the route at delegation. A `reasoning_effort` call argument overrides it. |
| `subagentProvider` | `spawn` | Subagent execution backend, not the LLM provider. |
| `maxDepth` | `3` | Maximum delegation depth enforced by the back

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Settings reference：Every field is volatile. The delegation tool is always named `subagent_model`; a legacy `toolName` field is ignored.

The live catalog is advisory: some adapters accept model ids they do not advertise. Manually entered ids remain allowed but should be user-confirmed.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Known limitations：The native session-header subagent catalog shows no model chip: DSH 0.1.7 has no additive slot inside a catalog row, and this release no longer replaces the host's `subagent-catalog` cell. The `subagent-model` header chip is still registered at `priority: -1` so a host build that also fills that cell stays shadowed rather than clashing.

dsh-subagent-model-router README · Known limitations：Better Sidebar's public tab registry is the supported integration seam. The router does not scrape foreign DOM, inject into native Tasks rows, or modify Better Sidebar source. The registered tab is optional and scoped to the service lifecycle; if Better Sidebar is unavailable, native headers, catalogs, settings, and model chips continue unchanged.
